To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a DCNN based DIQA approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, b) a two stage fine tuning approach can be used to transfer deep knowledge from a pre-trained model to a new task, and c) the proposed approach can be applied to other image quality assessment problems as well.
a DCNN trained on a large dataset of natural scene images can be fine tuned and applied on a new task, namely, document image quality assessment.
a deep transfer learning approach to document image quality assessment can achieve state-of-the-art performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a deep transfer learning approach for the problem of document image quality assessment and we believe it will be of interest to the research community working in this area.
the development of a novel deep transfer learning based DIQA model which is trained in a supervised manner using only the document images without any ground truth quality scores.
the application of deep transfer learning in the field of document image quality assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is a state of the art model for DIQA and it is also a good example of a deep transfer learning based approach to solve a new task using knowledge from a different domain.
this work presents the first no reference DIQA method based on DCNNs, and the proposed method achieves state of theart performance on a benchmark dataset.
the proposed model outperforms all the existing models on the considered benchmark dataset by a large margin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a deep transfer learning procedure can be successfully applied for the task of no reference document image quality assessment, where the rich knowledge base of a previously trained deep network can be exploited to facilitate a task specific network to learn the task in a much more efficient way.

the proposed approach can be used to transfer knowledge learned from a large scale natural scene image database for a specific OCR application to another OCR application with a different document image database.
we have demonstrated a deep transfer learning approach to DIQA that can be easily extended to other applications such as document restoration and OCR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep transfer learning is a promising approach for the problem of no reference DIQA.
the rich knowledge of the pre-trained DCNN is effectively transferred to the new task of DIQA.
the rich knowledge base of a DCNN trained for natural scene image quality assessment is transferable to document images and can be effectively utilized for document image quality assessment.
